provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Generator mechanism: the grid is random 0/5 noise. Four non-overlapping 3x3 boxes are stamped into it. Each box has a 5 centre and 8 cells that are each 5 or 2, so a box never contains a 0. The output turns every non-red box cell into 7 and the centre into 4. The constructor guarantees four things: (a) each box has 1 to 6 reds; (b) reds from different boxes are more than 3 apart in Chebyshev distance; (c) the noise contains no 2s; (d) no other 0-free, non-red-centred 3x3 window within distance 2 of the true centre holds the same number of reds. Together these mean a group's reds lie within Chebyshev 2 of each other. Union-find on the reds with Chebyshev distance <= 2 therefore recovers exactly one group per box. Any window that contains all of a group's reds must be centred within distance 2 of the true centre. It also cannot contain reds from another group, because two reds in one window are at most 2 apart. So the true centre is the unique in-bounds 3x3 window that contains the whole group, has a background centre and contains no 0. The emitted program enumerates only the windows that cover the group's bounding box and applies that test. It then stamps the frame (non-red cells become palette[7]) and the centre (palette[4]). The rule is invariant under D4: Chebyshev grouping, square windows and the test are all symmetric. So d4 needs no axis or direction specialisation, and the program works directly in visible coordinates. Colour roles are fixed as the constants palette[0] (blocker), palette[2] (red), palette[5] (background), palette[4] (centre) and palette[7] (frame). This matches the archived solver on all supplied fixtures. The archived solver's extra 5x5-ring check is implied by the constructor's spacing, so the program does not include it.
draft_notes.limitations: Tie handling: if a group had more than one qualifying window, the program stamps nothing for that group. It does not pick one by scan order, because scan order depends on orientation. The constructor's uniqueness check plus the red-spacing rule rule out ties inside its domain, so this branch should never fire. Outside the domain, the following cases would also be stamped nothing: noise containing 2s, red groups that cannot be separated at Chebyshev distance 2, or groups spanning more than 3 cells. Colour roles come from the palette constants, not from the demonstrations, and the palette is assumed to be a bijection. Constructor note for host review: the draw() function never checks that the stamped centre cell is non-red. This is safe only because the scene sampler always forces that centre to 5. Its uniqueness loop also skips candidate centres that are out of bounds (outside rows and columns 1 to 17), which is consistent with windows having to fit inside the grid. I found no contradiction between the fixtures and the uniform rule. No tests were run.
